chunks: And in the narration of Abān, from ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, he said:

Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام performed ghusl at Dhū al-Ḥulayfah for ihram, and prayed. Then he said, 'Bring what you have of the meat of game.' So two partridges were brought to him, and he ate them before entering ihram.

key_terms.الْإِحْرَامِ: the consecrated state for hajj or ʿumrah
key_terms.يُحْرِمَ: to enter the state of ihram

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat game before entering the state of ihram?
ai.summary: This narration describes Imām al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام performing ghusl and salat at Dhū al-Ḥulayfah in preparation for ihram. It also shows that he ate game meat before actually entering the state of ihram, indicating a practical distinction between preparation for ihram and the commencement of its restrictions.
